Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/15/2023
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack. Neither the well operator or permit number is posted on the well or well site.This well is plumbed into a 2000 gallon plastic tank located next to the well. The upper portion of this tank is cracked/broken. This tank is approximately one-third full with production fluid from the well, including crude oil. There is no containment in place around this tank.The specific conductance (SPC) of the soil in the proximity of the valve for this tank and a smaller tote adjacent to the tank is elevated. In addition to elevated SPC, the soil is stained, vegetation is stressed and deer tracks are abundant near the tank and tote. The SPC of standing water and soil in the roadside ditch that runs next to the tank is also elevated for approximately 200 feet both to the north and south of the tank.The access road between this well and 053-29570 has not been properly maintained. As a result, the installed BMPs are not functional and accelerated erosion of the road surface has occurred. Numerous other sections of lease roads throughout the Warrant 2878 lease have also been neglected and are in need of repair/maintenance to be considered in compliance.Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material at this well site.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/02/2025 to K PETROLEUM INC in Nottingham Township, Washington county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation ID: 8250813
Permit API: 125-22538
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Nottingham Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/02/2025
Comments: On October 2, 2025, the Department conducted a Routine Complete Inspection of K Petroleum Inc's Patterson 1 well site located in Nottingham Township, Washington County.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag with all required information posted on it fixed to the wellhead on site. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a meter box and separator on site. The meter box was observed to have a well posting fixed to it with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this meter box and separator.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a production tank within an earthen dike. An approximately 6 ft by 4 ft area on the ground at the base of the production tank where the valve is located was observed to be lacking vegetative cover. Pieces of the valve appeared to be broken off and was observed to be laying on the ground adjacent to the production tank. At the time of this inspection, an orange sheeny substance was observed to be actively dripping from the valve onto the ground around the production tank. The ground in this area was observed to be stained a dark black color with pooling of the orange substance observed directly below the valve. At the time of this inspection the Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the ground in this release area. Soil conductivity readings of 0.460 mS, 0.237 mS, 0.329 mS, and 0.308 mS were collected and compared to a background soil conductivity readings of 0.0635 mS collected in a vegetated area adjacent to the well site. These soil conductivity readings are elevated when compared to the background soil conductivity reading, which further subjugates that a release has occurred in this area. While on site, the Department called the number listed on the well tag/well posting as well as K Petroleum Inc's Robert Inghram. The Department was not able to reach either via phone, therefore the Department left a voicemail for each regarding the findings during today's inspection.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based one today's inspection, violations are being issued for a release from the production tank.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-01-10 to Chevron Appalachia Llc in South Huntingdon Twp, Westmoreland county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Chevron Appalachia Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-01-10
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 873926
Permit API: 129-28979
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: South Huntingdon Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2020-01-10
Comments: As documented in Inspection Record #2971125, the self-reported amount of oil-based mud released was 5 barrels (see Spill/Release Information of Photo #2). The Department recommended remediating the spill pursuant to §78a66(c)2 in an Inspection received by the operator on December 13, 2019. As of January 10, 2019, a satisfactory initial written report pursuant to §78a66(c)2 has not been received. The report provided by the operator on December 12, 2019 and documented in Inspection Record #2971125 only satisfies §78a66(c)2(i)(A), (C), and (F). Inspection Records #2970703 and #2971139 shows petroleum-based mud in multiple locations on the pad. Inspection Record #2971139 shows an unknown substance with a rainbow sheen discharging from under secondary containment at least 100 feet from the well heads. The Department collected multiple sample on the site on December 6, 2019. Sample results show the petroleum-based mud in an erosion rill greater than 200 feet from the well heads. The rill is on the edge of the well pad and discharges toward a stormwater channel which leads to the PCSM forebay; this evidence is sufficient to not only show the extent of the spill, but also that the spilled material has left the well pad and entered stormwater facilities. Per a telephone conversation with Chevron representative B. A. Lambie on January 8, 2020, the initial remediation by Chevron was completed on December 9, 2019. Department personnel were on-site on December 9, 2019 as documented in Inspection Record #298131. At the time of inspection, secondary containment was still in place. A strong petroleum odor and non-bacterial sheen were observed near and in stormwater channel R-4, respectively. The Department collected multiple samples from the site on December 27, 2019. The rill and nearby areas had not been altered as of December 27, 2019, nor had channel R-4. Sample results from December 27, 2019 show hexane is present in at least three locations in the material spilled near the pad entrance as mentioned in Inspection Record #2970703. The spilled material will need remediated pursuant to §78a66(c). At this time, hexane is being treated as a separate spill. Additional violations are being issued. Photographs are referenced as part of the operator-provided inspections provided on December 16, 2019 as requested in Inspection Record #2971139. However, the photographs cannot be accessed. Therefore, the inspections provided were incomplete. The photographs were requested via e-mail on December 17, 2019. As of January 10, 2019, the photographs have not been provided. Additional violations may be forthcoming based on review of the complete inspections. In Inspection Record #2971139, the Department requested photographic documentation of the removal of the secondary containment that remained on December 6, 2019 be provided by December 27, 2019. As of January 10, 2019, the documentation has not been provided.

Violation ID: 8197008
Permit API: 051-23285
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Dunbar Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/06/2024
Comments: On August 6 2024, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Nelson 2 OG Well in Dunbar Township, Fayette County. At the time of the inspection, the well appeared to be equipped for production. The well posting was present at the time of the inspection.The access road appeared to be stable with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with the exception of the affected area of the pump jack fluid release documented in inspection reports 3552812 and 3728744. There were erosion and sedimentation issues at the well site and adjacent to the wellhead due to the prior releases of the fluid from the pump jack onto the ground in inspection reports 3552812 and 3728744. It appears the erosion that previously extended adjacent to and downslope from the well site is now exhibiting greater than 70% vegetative coverage with the exception of the area between the agricultural fence adjacent to the well site and the wellhead ;this area is located approximately 10ft to 15ft from the wellhead. A background soil conductivity reading was taken. The soil conductivity reading was 0.0370mS. Soil conductivity readings were taken around the wellhead. The soil conductivity readings were 0.883mS, 0.273mS, 0.407mS, and 0.464mS. Although soil conductivity readings around the wellhead with visually stained gravel were lower compared to previous inspections, these readings are still higher than the background soil conductivity reading. It appears visually that the area around the wellhead and area extending approximately 10ft to 15ft from the wellhead are not remediated due to the stained gravel, the lack of vegetation, and high conductivity readings.The area between the agricultural fence adjacent to the well site and the wellhead ;this area is located approximately 10ft to 15ft from the wellhead had soil conductivity readings of 4.71mS and 5.46mS. Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was from the secondary containment of a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. All contaminated soil was removed from the site and the clean up area was top soiled and stabilized with seed and mulch. All disturbed area restored with a good growth of vegetation growing in October until cold weather. A ditch was cut west through the field from the culvert discharge with no E&S controls which has resulted in erosion of the ditch. E&S controls have been installed on this site in the areas of concentrated flow. There are still several areas in the restored area that show evidence of concentrated flow and erosion. These areas, as well as the entire restored site need to be inspected and maintained until there is enough vegetation growth to stabilize the area. The report for the clean-up and restoration of the area needs to be submitted to the Department and approved before violations can be lifted.

Comments: On April 30, 2026 the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation of Diversified's Yasenosky 2 plugged gas well site located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following IR 4111999, where violations were issued for failure to comply with a COA of the Department for failing to restore the plugged well site and access road.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on March 7, 2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the site within 9 months of well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. At the time of this inspection, a Well Site Restoration Report with a landowner waiver of site restoration has yet to be received. During IR 4168113, the Department observed an empty mailbox on the ground at the access road entrance, however, at the time of this inspection, a site restoration plan was observed to be within the mailbox. Refer to IR 4190625 for the closure of violations associated with failure to have the site restoration plan on site. At the time of this inspection, the access road was observed to still be graveled and unrestored with no erosion and sedimentation issues observed. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the plugged gas well site to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion and sedimentation issues observed. CFS appeared to be spread and removed from the perimeter of the plugged well site. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for failure to comply with the COA for failing to restore the plugged well site and access road is to remain outstanding at this time as the access road is still unrestored and a WSRR with a signed landowner waiver requesting the access road remain has yet to be received.

Violation ID: 878220
Permit API: 047-24535
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Saint Marys City
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-02-19
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report of a possible spill/breached containment at the Beechwood Pad A site. (CTS #348135). The site was inspected for evidence of lack of secondary containment around equipment and/or spills. The production fluid tank site was inspected. This site contains three 400 barrel tanks. It appears from the staining on the tanks that they have overflowed at some point. The containment is filled with snow that has not fully melted. The area behind (on the north side) of the tank site was checked and there was some liquid beneath the ice in the ditch. This liquid measured between 2 mS/cm to over 6 mS/cm conductivity on the Spectrum Soil EC probe. It appears as though a leak occurred at this site at some point, which the operator allowed to escape containment through some means and enter the ditch line. The overflow detection system appears to have been turned off at this tank site. Also on site was a gas/liquid separator which was fed by several types of fluid. The fluids were contained in their separate containments. The separator was set in containment that had blocks set up for holding tanks that have been removed. The containment itself was dry and it was noted that there were several holes in the liner, which would allow any spilled fluid to leak out of containment. The area around the wellheads is clean and no evidence of spills was noted. The site ID sign is on site with well and pad information.

Comments: On June 22 2023, the Department conducted an inspection of the Prigg Morgan 11272 Well Site due to an incident. Accompaying in today's inspection was Derek Zofchak (Range Resource Representative), Nick Reda (Range Resource Representative) and Tyler Metzger (ET DEP)The findings were as follows:This inspection is in response to several E and S BMP failures on the Prigg Morgan Well Site. In a phone call from Range Resource Representative Dennis Furmacek, they reported that they had 3 separate sections of temporary E and S BMP silt sox were overtopped and or displaced. This resulted in sediment to leave the LOD and settle into adjacent vegetative field. The failures were identified during a post precipitation inspection conducted on 6/16/2023. Mr. Furmacek also indicated that waters of the commonwealth were not threatened and sediment was not discharged into the waters of the commonwealth. During today's inspection, the Act 9 Sign was on site but not permanently installed. The access road appeared to be stable with no observed erosion or sedimentation concerns. The ESCGP drawings, PPC plan and ER plan were on site. Also on site was the site inspection records for 6/16/2023 recording the E and S BMP silt sox overtopping and 6/19/2023 which recorded the remediation efforts at the well site. The CFS that was effected in the three different locations were all re-staked. Each area that was affected outside of the LOD were mulched and reseeded.Based on today's inspection, The Department will conduct a subsequent inspection to continue to evaluate remediation efforts.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a third party report of crude oil accumulated outside of the tank battery located at this well site.Upon my arrival, I observed a steel stock tank within an earthen containment located behind a conventional well that is equipped with a pump jack. There are currently no appreciable accumulations evident inside of the containment. There is evidence of recent earth disturbance along the western wall of the earthen containment. Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/07/2020
Comments: On October 5, 2020, I conducted a follow up inspection of the Fred Jones Well Site in Independence Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the Department on 10/4/2020 (CID#352896) . The 10/4/2020 report indicated that approximately 630 gallons of brine was spilled to the well pad. I spoke with Operator representative Casey Barkus on 10/5/2020. Mr. Barkus indicated that a non-structural weld developed a pin hole in the brine tank and caused a stream of brine to shoot across the well pad. Mr. Barkus indicated that the release continued until the brine could be removed from the brine tank. Mr. Barkus indicated that the brine was contained on the well pad and that the pad drain valves were closed. Mr. Barkus indicated that the operator would be utilizing Act 2 clean up as a remediation standard.At the time of inspection, I spoke with operator Josh Boyda. The operator was utilizing third party contractors Miller Environmental and Moody and Associates to guide the remediation of the impacted area. The operator was utilizing a skid steer and excavator to removed impacted material. Mr. Boyda indicated that the impacted material has been placed in the roll off boxes and the crew is awaiting additional disposal boxes to be delivered. I observed 5 rolloff boxes staged within secondary containment and 2 more rolloff boxes located near the impacted area. Mr. Boyda indicated that approximately 12 yards of impacted material has been placed in each rolloff box. The impacted area appeared to be 100' x 60' area located between the brine tank battery and the fenced in well head area. Approximately 6” of material had been removed from the impacted area. Mr. Boyda showed me the non-structural weld on the brine tank that caused the release. The weld in question is located on the brine tank approximately 6' from the bottom of tank on the left side of the brine tank manufacturer information plate.I utilized a Spectrum Field Scout Direct Soil EC meter to screen for conductivity. I screened the impacted area, outlet location and the standing water within the pad drain system.At the impacted area near the fenced well head the meter indicated conductivity of 8.75 mS/cm.At the approximately center of the impacted area of the well pad the meter indicated conductivity of 12.80 mS/cm.At the storm water inlet in the northwest corner of the well pad the meter indicated that conductivity was Or (Or is over range. The meter's max conductivity limit is 20 mS/cm).At the outlet of the pad drain on the meter indicated that conductivity was 0.5 mS/cm.The pad drain outlet appeared to be closed. Comments: On October 5, 2020, I conducted a follow up inspection of the Fred Jones Well Site in Independence Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the Department on 10/4/2020 (CID#352896) . The 10/4/2020 report indicated that approximately 630 gallons of brine was spilled to the well pad. I spoke with Operator representative Casey Barkus on 10/5/2020. Mr. Barkus indicated that a non-structural weld developed a pin hole in the brine tank and caused a stream of brine to shoot across the well pad. Mr. Barkus indicated that the release continued until the brine could be removed from the brine tank. Mr. Barkus indicated that the brine was contained on the well pad and that the pad drain valves were closed. Mr. Barkus indicated that the operator would be utilizing Act 2 clean up as a remediation standard.At the time of inspection, I spoke with operator Josh Boyda. The operator was utilizing third party contractors Miller Environmental and Moody and Associates to guide the remediation of the impacted area. The operator was utilizing a skid steer and excavator to removed impacted material. Mr. Boyda indicated that the impacted material has been placed in the roll off boxes and the crew is awaiting additional disposal boxes to be delivered. I observed 5 rolloff boxes staged within secondary containment and 2 more rolloff boxes located near the impacted area. Mr. Boyda indicated that approximately 12 yards of impacted material has been placed in each rolloff box. The impacted area appeared to be 100' x 60' area located between the brine tank battery and the fenced in well head area. Approximately 6” of material had been removed from the impacted area. Mr. Boyda showed me the non-structural weld on the brine tank that caused the release. The weld in question is located on the brine tank approximately 6' from the bottom of tank on the left side of the brine tank manufacturer information plate.I utilized a Spectrum Field Scout Direct Soil EC meter to screen for conductivity. I screened the impacted area, outlet location and the standing water within the pad drain system.At the impacted area near the fenced well head the meter indicated conductivity of 8.75 mS/cm.At the approximately center of the impacted area of the well pad the meter indicated conductivity of 12.80 mS/cm.At the storm water inlet in the northwest corner of the well pad the meter indicated that conductivity was Or (Or is over range. The meter's max conductivity limit is 20 mS/cm).At the outlet of the pad drain on the meter indicated that conductivity was 0.5 mS/cm.The pad drain outlet appeared to be closed. Comments: On 12/18/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the John Briggs Well pad in Aleppo Township, Greene County for a reported release (CTS: 394097). They were all observed to be below clean up standards (Photos 8-12).It appears the spill still needs additional remediation in certain areas. The Department requests information on the amount spilled and how the amount was verified.Violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued for the spill.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/16/2024
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8183692
Permit API: 129-28483
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Sewickley Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/16/2024
Comments: On April 16th, 2024 the Department conducted a routine inspection of EQT's Cook Well Pad located in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County. Accompanying in today's inspection is Samantha Foulk (WQSS DEP).At the time of the inspection, the Act 9 sign was present at the entrance of the access road and the ERP was present in the onsite mailbox.There are 2 total wells on this well pad that appeared to be equipped for production and are surrounded by cement barriers. Well 17H's well tag as present at the time of inspection with all necessary information posted and no fluid discharges were observed from/near the wellhead. The 17H GPU was surrounded by cement barriers but was not in secondary containment. Well 17H has a SPUD date prior to the October 2016 promulgation of Chapter 78a, therefore secondary containment is not required to be installed. Staining of the gravel below the piping of the 17H GPU was observed. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the edge of the well site along the chainlink fence (0.186 mS) as a background, and then three others were taken at the base of the GPU piping where the discoloration can be seen (0.021 mS, 0.002 mS and 0.013 mS). These readings were comparable to the background and therefore are not indicative of a release.The 17H production tank was in secondary containment that had fluid pooled in it and was surrounded by cement barriers. A conductivity reading of the fluid within was 0.158 mS. The production tank appeared to be sound with no observable leaks or discharge. The Department recommends the Operator monitor the secondary containment to ensure that the fluid currently in it will not inhibit its 110% hold capacity requirements.The access road and well pad appeared to be stabilized. Upon inspection of the perimeter of the well site, at least 70% vegetative growth was seen throughout as well as two riprap aprons. The riprap apron at the front of the well site did not show any erosion or sedimentation concerns, however the riprap apron at the rear of the well site did exhibit concerns. The rear riprap apron appeared to be improperly implemented and/or maintained to adequately prevent channelized flow from forming. Approximately 45-50 feet of channelized flow containing sediment was observed going from the end of the riprap apron outlet to an agricultural field nearby. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the riprap apron outlet to prevent any further erosion from occurring. With the exception of this area of concern, the remainder of the well site appeared to exhibit greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth.Based on todays inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to maintain PCSM BMPs.Prior to leaving the location, the Department notified Operator representative Logan Dominick of the above-noted concern, who responded that they would promptly address it.

Comments: The site of this oil spill is in a forested area on an access road south off Center Hill Road, 430 yards on south branch of access. Will Warfel contacted WQS Taylor and reported to National Response Center that there was a release of about 20 gallons of crude oil from a tank the wind tipped over in one of the recent storms. The path of the crude oil was ~320 yards on the access from origin of the spill to low spot where it left the road and seeped into the stream. Blobs of oily material were found ~60 yards downstream. Two absorbent booms were placed in the stream along with absorbent pads. One absorbent boom was placed across the access road and one was positioned along the road to catch any remaining oil from seeping to stream. Visual clean-up of oil and oil contaminated soil completed where the tank tipped and leaked oil. The tank was removed and contaminated soil piled and covered until soil is tested and can be received at a licensed facility.Violations for the release of oil to ground and into a stream issued with this inspection. Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after multiple releases on Pad B for which violations remain outstanding. Both pads and the access road were snow-covered during this inspection. The completions operations have ceased on Pad B and the snubbing rigs and their associated equipment have been removed from the pad. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad B. A representative from Creston Environmental was present on location as well. A crew was working on installing the GPUs on the pad. Trenches were being dug for the flow lines which will run from the well heads to the GPUs on the west side of the pad. A large trench was present at the well heads. Some fluid was seeping into this trench from the fill material surrounding the well cellar for well B-11H. The electrical conductivity (EC) of this fluid was 2.45 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was sucking up this fluid during this inspection. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up any elevated EC fluid found on the pad surface or during excavation on the pad. The modular aboveground storage structure (MASS) was empty during this inspection. A work crew was beginning to disassemble the MASS during this inspection. The north central area of the well pad has been excavated. One area is a long horizontal area approximately two feet of the north stormwater channel. The EC of the fluid here was 3.35 to 5.41 mS/cm. Another excavated area is to the southwest. According to Mr. Subra, EQT believes that the produced fluid that had been released to this area flowed along an area that had previously been excavated in association with a release that occurred during drilling operations on the well pad. Mr. Subra also said that the northwest area of the well pad where clamshell boxes had led to a release in the dancefloor area has been fully excavated. Additional excavation would still need to occur in the north central area of the well pad as well as in the northeast corner of the pad where the MASS still is present, he also stated. The lined sump remains at the east outlet of the north stormwater channel.Violations remain outstanding for the release of produced fluid to the northwest area of Pad B from clam shell boxes in the area of the dancefloor.

Violation ID: 8276969

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/04/2026
Comments: On 06/03/2026 at 0017 hours the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) received a notification of a release at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County (CTS #398207). Representative Ralph Babcock stated "on 6/2/26 at 5:15 p.m., a Keystone Clear Water truck driver was loading production water when the line split releasing 25 gallons of produced water. Approximately 10 gallons of produced water spilled into a containment structure while the remaining 15 gallons of produced water spilled onto the ground. Keystone Clearwater vacuumed produced water from the containment structure and scraped up impacted soil for later disposal.The DEP contacted Repsol and spoke with Mr. Babcock at 1145 hours. He stated the material from the release had been recovered and placed in drums onsite. He stated the release took place in the off-loading area of the pad. He stated he was notified of the released at 2345 hours (06/02).On 06/04/2026 the DEP conducted an incident inspection. I arrived at 0915 hours and met with Mr. Babcock. Environmental Resources was onsite to collect samples from the release and the prior release (CTS#396090). The area of the release was ~33 feet long (photo #2). There were no pooled fluids in the area of the release. Fluids on the pad surface were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 452-1042 us/cm. The cause of the release was due to a valve malfunction (photo #3). Environmental resources screened the soil in the area of the release and received readings of 1-1.3 mS/cm (1000-1300 us/cm). The recovered material was observed in drums onsite and held within secondary containment (photo #4).The DEP screened the area of the prior release (CTS #396090). Fluids within the stormwater ditch at the release point were field measured for EC at ~452 us/cm. Mr. Babcock stated that this week there would be more material removed from the stormwater ditch at the release point due to elevated soil readings. There was dead vegetation observed downgrade of the affected bio-retention basin (photo #15-16). Fluids within and directly upgrade of the furthest downgrade sump pump were measured for EC between 1.248-2.24 mS/cm (1248-2240 us/cm) (photo #17 and 18). Fluids downgrade of the sump pump were field measured for EC between 173.7-398 us/cm. The violations related to the recent spill (CTS #398207) are considered immediately corrected however, outstanding violations remain open for API#015-23994 from the previous release (CTS #396090).I departed at 1120 hours.
